results.title: National Minimum Wage / social care essay
results.known: 19–20 out of 25, marked by the teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-13). Originally reported only as "mid A", which is a grade band rather than a mark — the real figure was obtained rather than inferred from a grade boundary, since guessing it and then treating the guess as ground truth is exactly the substitution this project exists to prevent. Kept as a range, which is honest, rather than forced to one number.

issues.text: The claim that an increase in the national minimum wage would increase market failure (e.g., 'Additionally, an increase in national minimum wage would increase market failure') is incorrect because wage increases do not directly create market failure; market failure arises from externalities, not wage changes.

The explanation of the subsidy effect is vague and lacks a clear causal chain (e.g., 'By subsidising wages, firms would therefore be able to maintain profitability due to lower costs of production...').

results.improvement: Add a clear causal explanation that a wage subsidy reduces the wage component of MC, shifting the MC curve downwards and restoring profitability.
